children.value: > Fact From Story The report found that Arabic content was flagged as potentially violating at significantly higher rates than Hebrew content was, and was more likely to be erroneously removed.

> > Fact From Story The report noted that Meta’s moderation system may not be as precise for Arabic content as it was for Hebrew content, because the latter is a “more standardized language,” and suggested that reviewers may lack the linguistic and cultural competence to understand less common Arabic dialects like Palestinian Arabic.

> > > Fact From Story Meta struggles to navigate the cultural and linguistic nuances of Arabic, a language with over 25 dialects, and has been criticized for neglecting to adequately diversify its language resources.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge If a system struggles with a language, it will have difficulty moderating content in that language effectively.
> > Commonsense Knowledge Flagging content as violating community standards restricts freedom of expression.

> Fact From Story A report commissioned by Meta and conducted by a third party concluded that the company’s actions had an “adverse human rights impact” on Palestinian users’ right to freedom of expression and political participation.
> > Fact From Story Users have also complained that they’ve been harassed and reported for posting content about Palestine, regardless of whether or not it violates Meta’s policies.

> > > Fact From Story Meta forbids support of terrorist organizations, like most social media companies based in the U.S., but struggles to moderate content around it, from user discourse to journalistic updates.
> > > Fact From Story The restrictions on content, especially the content that relates to Palestine, is heavily politicized.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Restrictions and moderation of content can have an adverse impact on freedom of expression and political participation.
